cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: test coverage sits at 31%, there is no coverage gate in continuous integration, and production systems of comparable complexity typically run 40-60% coverage.
cases.output: Test coverage sits at 31%, with no coverage gate in continuous integration. Production systems of comparable complexity typically maintain 40 to 60% coverage. The gap means regressions can reach production unchallenged, and the lack of an automated gate removes a standard safeguard against degradation.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: deployments are performed manually by one engineer via SSH, there is no rollback procedure, and the last rollback attempt (8 months ago) took over 3 hours to complete.
cases.output: The most recent rollback attempt, 8 months ago, took over 3 hours to complete, and deployments are otherwise performed manually by a single engineer via SSH with no documented rollback procedure. This creates a single point of failure in the deployment process with no mitigation in place. A regression reaching production would require manual intervention by that one engineer to reverse, with no tested process to guide the work and no parallel capacity to maintain availability during the remediation.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: one engineer holds sole access to the production database credentials, there is no documented access-handover process, and that engineer is on a rolling month-to-month contract.
cases.output: Production database credentials are held by a single engineer on a rolling month-to-month contract, with no documented access-handover process. If that engineer departs or becomes unavailable, the company loses access to its production data until credentials can be rotated and reissued—a process that has never been executed and lacks documented procedure. There is no compensating control. We recommend establishing credential rotation procedures, distributing production database access across a minimum of two engineers, and documenting the handover steps required when contract staff depart.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) using these facts only: customer personal data is retained indefinitely with no deletion policy, and there is no documented process for handling a data-subject deletion request.
cases.output: Customer personal data is retained indefinitely with no documented deletion policy or process for handling data-subject deletion requests. This creates exposure under GDPR Article 17 and similar regulations, where individuals have a right to erasure that the company cannot currently fulfill. The company has no compensating control. Data accumulates without bounds, and a breach would affect an ever-growing population of individuals.

cases.input: Write one due-diligence finding paragraph (3-5 sentences) covering ALL of these facts: test coverage is 31%, there is no CI coverage gate, the last three production incidents were caused by untested edge cases, deployments are manual, and there is no rollback procedure. Do not omit any fact.
cases.output: Test coverage stands at 31%, with no coverage gate in continuous integration to block regressions. Of the last 3 production incidents, all 3 were caused by untested edge cases. Deployments are performed manually by engineers with SSH access, and there is no documented rollback procedure. This combination leaves the system exposed to defects that testing would catch, with no automated safeguard and no fast path to recover if a deployment fails.

cases.input: Write three separate due-diligence findings, one paragraph each, clearly separated by a blank line. Finding 1 facts: passwords are stored in plaintext in the users table. Finding 2 facts: deployments are manual with no rollback procedure. Finding 3 facts: code comment style is inconsistent across the codebase, with no linting rule enforcing a convention.
cases.output:
Passwords are stored in plaintext in the users table, with no hashing or salting applied. This means any attacker who gains database access obtains valid credentials for every user account immediately. There is no compensating control. We recommend implementing bcrypt or a similar algorithm, with a migration plan for existing credentials and a requirement that all new password changes use the new scheme.

Deployments are performed manually with no documented or tested rollback procedure. The company has no automated deployment tooling and no staging environment for pre-production validation. This creates a direct path from human error to production outage, and an outage becomes a prolonged incident if a rollback attempt fails. We recommend establishing an automated deployment pipeline with a tested rollback path and a staging environment that mirrors production.

Code comment style varies across the codebase with no enforcement mechanism. A review of a 40,000-line service found single-line comments using eight different formats, and inline documentation for complex logic is missing in roughly a third of modules where it would aid maintenance. This is a code-health issue rather than a security or availability concern, but it raises the cognitive load on engineers and slows onboarding. We recommend adopting a single comment style, enforcing it with a linter rule, and documenting the convention in the contribution guidelines.
